question: When does Gong pay for itself in coaching ROI?
answer:
**Gong ROI timeline: rep productivity +3–5% by month 4 (pays for itself), +8–12% by month 12 if you use it for coaching, not just compliance.** Cost: $50–100K annually for 50 reps. Payoff: $500K–1M in incremental ARR at 75% GM. But only if your manager coaches using it (if you just record, ROI is zero). **How Gong generates ROI:** 1. **Call coaching (month 1–4).** Managers watch 2–3 calls per rep per week, identify gaps (not asking discovery questions, missing objection handling, forgot to close). In 4 weeks, reps stop making the same mistake. Delta: +2–3% close rate. 2. **Deal strategy (month 5–8).** Gong's conversation intelligence scores buyer sentiment (customer says "budget" or "timeline" 5x = they're getting serious). Reps know which deals to push. Delta: +2–4% pipeline velocity. 3. **Competitive intelligence (month 9–12).** Your reps call accounts where competitors are entrenched. Gong transcripts show you what competitor pitched, objections your reps faced. Sales leadership writes playbook to counter. Delta: +2–3% win rate against specific competitors. **What kills Gong ROI:** - No manager coaching time allocated. If Gong is "just recording," reps never see the insight. ROI is zero. - Managers watch full calls (60 min) instead of clips (8 min). By month 2, they stop watching. - Recording without intent (legal-compliance only, no coaching workflow). You're paying for filing cabinet. **The coaching workflow that actually works:** 1. **Manager sets 10-min weekly coaching cadence.** Every Thursday 4–4:10 PM: manager + rep review one Gong clip (Gong auto-surfaces high-opportunity clips). 2. **Focus on ONE skill per rep per week.** "This week: let's nail your discovery question," not "improve everything." 3. **Clip + action.** Manager shows 2-min clip, rep commits to change. Manager follows up next call. Delta: visible improvement by week 3. 4. **Rollup:** Manager summarizes top 3 coaching themes (discovery weakness, objection handling, closing) and teaches team in standup. **ROI calculation:** | Input | Value | |-------|-------| | 50 reps × 5 calls/week | 250 calls/week | | Gong license (annual) | $75,000 | | Manager coaching (4 hrs/week) | Allocated | | Rep productivity lift (month 1–4) | +3% | | New ARR from lift | $600K (60 reps × $300K each ÷ 20 reps in motion) | | Payback period | 5 months | | Year-2 ROI | 8x | **When NOT to buy Gong:** - Sales team <15 reps. Cost per rep is $3,300+/year; can't justify coaching time. - Outbound-only team. Gong's AI is tuned for consultative selling (discovery, objection, close). Outbound cadence calls are transactional; Gong is overkill. - Sales cycle <2 weeks. No time to iterate on coaching. - No sales manager infrastructure (nobody to do coaching). Just gives you compliance tapes. **When Gong is a must-have:** - Enterprise sales motion (sales cycle 4–6 months). Every rep improvement = 10% pipeline move. - High new-rep turnover. Ramp-up cycle is 6+ months. Gong cuts it to 4. - Win rate <25%. Gong uncovers objection-handling gaps; usually lifts win rate 3–5%. **Action:** Pilot Gong for 4 reps × 2 months. Measure: do they improve on your key skill gap (discovery, objection, close)? If yes, roll out.
